exercises.title: Capacitors and RC Circuits: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: What is the time constant, and the time to reach 63.2% of the final value, for 10 kΩ charging a 10 µF capacitor from a step?
choices: τ = 100 ms, but 63.2% is reached at 500 ms
hints: τ = R × C; 63.2% is exactly one time constant.

exercises.title: Capacitors and RC Circuits: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Calculate the 10%, 63.2%, 90%, and 99% points for a 10 kΩ and 10 µF charging circuit.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

τ = RC = 10,000×10 µF = 0.100 s. Charging reaches 10% at −τ ln(0.9)=10.5 ms, 63.2% at 100 ms, 90% at 230 ms, and 99% at 461 ms. After 5τ=0.5 s the remaining error is about 0.67%. Probe resistance and capacitor leakage alter the measured curve.

The governing principle is: **select dielectric and rating from signal amplitude, bias, frequency, ripple, and accuracy needs**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Capacitors and RC Circuits: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **reversed electrolytic, ceramic capacitance loss under bias, missing discharge path, wrong time constant**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
